subject: Clarifying p95/p99 envelope and streaming concurrency — next technical checkpoints
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@veridian.ai>; Tom Lopez <t.lopez@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + clarifying asks from today’s perf call

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. High-level recap and the clarifying items we need to scope an apples-to-apples hosted vs incumbent p95/p99 probe: 

1) Acceptance envelope: you mentioned a target of p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 480ms for your live inference path (end-to-end, post-client aggregation). Please confirm whether those numbers are measured including client-side batching/merging or after server response only.

2) Traffic mix: we need the traffic split (text gen vs chat vs streaming) and the steady-state QPS plus spike profile (expected peak qps, burst duration). If you can share a 24h sample CSV with timestamps and request types that would be ideal — attached is the CSV template we prefer for parsing.

3) Streaming specifics: your team flagged long-lived streaming sessions with interleaved messages from multiple clients. Tell us if (a) streams are single-connection per user, (b) you use client-side multiplexing, and (c) typical concurrent stream count per connection. This changes how we model KV cache & per-stream concurrency.

4) Instrumentation & sampling: to validate p99 tail we recommend server-side span ids and request IDs in the sample CSV. Are you comfortable sharing limited anonymized IDs? Also confirm retention window for logs (we only need 48–72h for the probe).

Next steps I propose: we stand up a 48h hosted trial with mirrored traffic (or replay) and run a p95/p99 baseline vs your incumbent. Ben will own the test harness configuration, Marissa will track SLO acceptance criteria, and I’ll coordinate the mutual action plan.

Attachments: latency-metrics-veridian-p95p99.csv (template)

Can you confirm the three items above by EOD Monday? If anything from today’s call is missing here, call it out and I’ll update the MAP.

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

From: Samantha Park <samantha@veridian.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lopez <t.lopez@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying asks from today’s perf call

Thanks Logan — plus a couple clarifications inline. Good recap overall.

1) Acceptance envelope: the numbers I quoted (p95 220ms / p99 480ms) are measured end-to-end from our client SDK after we do client-side reassembly. So they include network + server + client-side merge. We can also provide server-only times if you need them — our tracing has both.

2) Traffic mix: attaching a 24h export (anonymized) and a short doc that maps request_type -> model_family. Peak observed: 2.2k qps sustained for ~3m during our morning batch window with micro-bursts up to ~3.8k qps for ~20s. Steady-state is ~650 qps.

3) Streaming specifics: streams are one connection per user, we do not multiplex multiple users on a single connection. Typical concurrent streams per connection is 1–3 (median 1). We do sometimes multiplex responses within a stream for real-time multi-message flows.

4) Instrumentation & sampling: we can share sampled request IDs (hashed) and server timestamps for 72h. Logs are retained for 7d on our side — 72h overlap is fine.

Attachments: veridian-24h-export-20270401.csv, veridian-request-to-model-map.pdf

Samantha
Samantha Park
Head of Platform Reliability | Veridian Health
samantha@veridian.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Park <samantha@veridian.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying asks from today’s perf call

Great data — thanks Sam. A few practical test/harness clarifications from my side: 

- Replay vs mirrored proxy: can we do a short mirrored window (10–15m) to validate end-to-end with live client aggregation, and a longer replay for stress profiles? Mirrored gives the realistic client assembly behavior.

- Concurrency knob: Redwood’s hosted runtime needs to know the intended per-instance concurrency budget and acceptable latency SLO tradeoff. For the probe we should test with: {concurrency=8, 16, 32} per worker and measure p95/p99. Can Veridian expose per-request CPU/seq-length metadata in the sample CSV? That helps with kernel selection.

- Streaming: we’ll exercise both short-lived streams and long-lived streams for 15m windows to observe KV cache warmup effects. Need an estimate for average stream lifespan — Sam, you mentioned some streams last 30s, others several minutes; a distribution would help.

I’ll draft the harness config and share by Monday: it will include exact request sampling, epoch durations, and the comparison matrix to run against incumbent.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Tom Lopez <t.lopez@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying asks from today’s perf call

Ben — quick answers to your bullets: 

- Mirrored window: yes, we can flip a proxy rule for a controlled 15m mirrored run next Wednesday (13:00 UTC).

- Concurrency: we can add per-request metadata (avg tokens, model_family, cpu_ms estimate) to the CSV for sampled requests. Expect sampling at ~0.5% of traffic by default — we can bump to 2% for the probe window.

- Stream lifespan distribution (rough): 55% < 60s, 30% between 60–300s, 15% > 300s. Typical concurrency per user connection peaks at ~3.

We’ll drop the mirrored run data into the shared Drive link and give you a read-only service account.

—
Tom Lopez
Lead SRE | Veridian Health

Perfect — thank you both. Short checklist / action items I’ll own and coordinate: 

1) Ben to circulate test harness config (by EOD Mon) — will include concurrency matrix, sample rates, and epoch durations.
2) Veridian to enable 15m mirrored run next Wed (13:00 UTC) and provide drive location + read-only SA.
3) Veridian to drop the sampled CSV with per-request metadata (0.5% -> 2% bump for probe) into the Drive; include server-only timestamps if possible.
4) Marissa to finalize SLO acceptance matrix (p95/p99 gates, tolerance bands, rollback criteria).
5) Logan to prepare MAP doc and upload mutual-action-plan-veridian.docx (shared) — will link to HubSpot deal RDW-4872 and schedule a post-probe sync for Thu morning.

I’ll attach the MAP and the template CSV now. If that schedule works I’ll send calendar invites for the mirror and the post-probe review.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the envelope with live traffic.
